synthesis.paragraph: The paper "Universal or local preferences? The perceived importance of the urban environment on active travel behaviour in Europe across populations" shares five references with the July 6 paper "Health, built environmental, and environmental perceptions in relation to non-commute walking among middle-aged adults," including "Travel demand and the 3Ds: Density, diversity, and design," "Built Environment Correlates of Walking," and "The built environment, walking, and physical activity: Is the environment more important to some people than others?". This same paper also shares four references with the July 8 paper "Nonlinear and interaction effects of the built environment on public bicycle usage: a case study of Taipei City非线性及建筑环境对公共自行车使用的影响：台北市的案例研究," and another four references with the July 9 paper "Beyond infrastructure: exploring drivers of subjective cycling safety using directed acyclic graphs (DAG)." The University of British Columbia appears on 2 of today's papers. Over the last 30 days, Hong Kong Polytechnic University appeared on 30 papers, Tongji University appeared on 29 papers, and both Tsinghua University and Peking University appeared on 20 papers.
